questions.chapter_title: Alkyl Halides: Nucleophilic Substitution and Elimination Reactions
questions.question: In the context of Alkyl Halides: Nucleophilic Substitution and Elimination Reactions, what is the major organic product when CH₃CH₂CH₂Br reacts under the following conditions: NaCN in anhydrous DMSO?
questions.explanation: Major product rationale: Unencumbered primary alkyl halide in polar aprotic solvent undergoes clean, rapid SN2 nucleophilic substitution. The correct major product is 'CH₃CH₂CH₂CN + NaBr'.

questions.chapter_title: Alkyl Halides: Nucleophilic Substitution and Elimination Reactions
questions.question: In the context of Alkyl Halides: Nucleophilic Substitution and Elimination Reactions, what is the major organic product when (CH₃)₃C-Br reacts under the following conditions: NaOCH₂CH₃ / EtOH at 60°C?
questions.explanation: Major product rationale: Strong unhindered base with tertiary substrate undergoes rapid E2 elimination without competing SN2 substitution. The correct major product is '(CH₃)₂C=CH₂ (Isobutylene) + EtOH + NaBr'.

questions.chapter_title: Alkyl Halides: Nucleophilic Substitution and Elimination Reactions
questions.question: In the context of Alkyl Halides: Nucleophilic Substitution and Elimination Reactions, what is the major organic product when 2-Bromobutane reacts under the following conditions: t-BuOK / t-BuOH at 75°C?
questions.explanation: Major product rationale: Bulky tert-butoxide base abstracts the more accessible, less hindered β-proton to yield 1-butene. The correct major product is '1-Butene (Major Hofmann product, ~80%)'.

questions.chapter_title: Alkyl Halides: Nucleophilic Substitution and Elimination Reactions
questions.question: In the context of Alkyl Halides: Nucleophilic Substitution and Elimination Reactions, what is the major organic product when 2-Bromobutane reacts under the following conditions: NaOEt / EtOH at 75°C?
questions.explanation: Major product rationale: Unhindered ethoxide base preferentially abstracts the internal β-hydrogen yielding the more stable trans-alkene. The correct major product is 'trans-2-Butene (Major Zaitsev product, ~70%)'.

questions.chapter_title: Alkyl Halides: Nucleophilic Substitution and Elimination Reactions
questions.question: In the context of Alkyl Halides: Nucleophilic Substitution and Elimination Reactions, what is the major organic product when (CH₃)₂CH-Br reacts under the following conditions: H₂O / Heat (solvolysis at 80°C)?
questions.explanation: Major product rationale: Solvolysis in polar protic water proceeds via ionization to secondary carbocation followed by water capture. The correct major product is '(CH₃)₂CH-OH + HBr'.

questions.chapter_title: Alkyl Halides: Nucleophilic Substitution and Elimination Reactions
questions.question: Which reaction conditions / reagents are required to convert (CH₃)₃C-Cl into (CH₃)₃C-OCH₃ (tert-Butyl methyl ether) + HCl in Alkyl Halides: Nucleophilic Substitution and Elimination Reactions?
questions.explanation: Reagent selection rationale: The transformation '(CH₃)₃C-Cl' → '(CH₃)₃C-OCH₃ (tert-Butyl methyl ether) + HCl' specifically requires 'CH₃OH (anhydrous, 25°C)'. Mechanistic basis: Unimolecular ionization of 3° chloride followed by nucleophilic capture by methanol solvent.

questions.chapter_title: Alkyl Halides: Nucleophilic Substitution and Elimination Reactions
questions.question: Which reaction conditions / reagents are required to convert CH₃I into CH₃-S-CH₃ (Dimethyl sulfide) + NaI in Alkyl Halides: Nucleophilic Substitution and Elimination Reactions?
questions.explanation: Reagent selection rationale: The transformation 'CH₃I' → 'CH₃-S-CH₃ (Dimethyl sulfide) + NaI' specifically requires 'NaSCH₃ in dry Acetone'. Mechanistic basis: Powerful, polarizable thiolate nucleophile rapidly displaces iodide via SN2.

questions.question: Which starting material yields '(Z)-1,2-Diphenylpropene' when treated with 'NaOEt / EtOH reflux' according to the principles of Alkyl Halides: Nucleophilic Substitution and Elimination Reactions?
